messages:
ana: Hey team, customer reported recurring p95 latency spikes during burst tests. They sent sample request IDs but we need a full repro manifest (curl + concurrency profile + token counts). Region: eu-west-1. Can someone own collection?

matt: I can grab the request IDs and run a controlled replay. do we want HAR or just curl scripts?

ana (typo correction): @matt — HAR + curl pack please. Also include the prompt set they used (they said a 3-step prompt chain with system->user->assistant). token counts per message are critical. :mag: 

matt: copying the request ids I already pulled: 0a1f7c2b, b3d9a8f0, d2f44c11. I'll produce a curl + small load script.

sasha: FYI infra-bot captured node logs for those IDs at 2026-12-09T14:21Z, path: /var/log/redwood/serve/eu-west-1/2026-12-09/*.gz (I will attach pointers). Some entries show KV cache misses around the spikes.

ryan: For replay, use a staircase pattern: 1->5->20 concurrent connections, 60s per step. Keep same prompt payloads and seed. That reproduces p95 more reliably than flat rps.

matt: curl example I'm going to include in the pack (replace <TOKEN>):

```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <TOKEN>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-xl-8k","input":"<USER_PROMPT>","max_tokens":256}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

matt: will also include a small k6 script that replays those exact bodies with concurrency knobs.

qa-jen: When you collect the prompt set, also include tokenized lengths per message (we have tokenization helpers in utils/token-count.py). If a message is >512 tokens it changes batching behavior.

ana: @sasha can you attach the node-level timeline slice (GPU utilization, queue depth, cache hitrate) for the three IDs? prefer csv or json.

sasha: attaching pointers and short excerpt:
`eu-west-1-node-7,2026-12-09T14:21:13, GPU: 84%, queue_len: 27, kv_cache_hits: 3/12`
`eu-west-1-node-3,2026-12-09T14:21:46, GPU: 92%, queue_len: 45, kv_cache_hits: 1/18`
(full logs in S3: s3://redwood-debug/eu-west-1/manifest-1834509123/)

ryan: Also log the model variant used. If the request fell back to the quantized shard (q4), latency diff will show. Provide model version hash + runtime kernel tag.

matt: Putting together debug bundle:
- prompts.json (raw prompt bodies)
- curls.sh (repeatable curl commands)
- replay-k6.js (staircase concurrency)
- token_counts.csv (per message breakdown)
- request_ids.txt
- node_timeline.csv (from infra)
- notes.md (what to watch: kv cache, kernel swaps, fallback events)

ana: Great. Plan: matt assemble bundle and upload to s3 path above. Then tag @eng-runtime to run a controlled replay in the staging pool with tracing enabled. If staging reproduces, open infra bug with attached traces.

matt: Upload complete: s3://redwood-debug/eu-west-1/manifest-1834509123/debug-bundle.tar.gz (sha256: e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb924). Added a short README with exact k6 command used.

infra-bot: Tracing toggle reminder: enable TRACE=1 and KERNEL_LOG_LEVEL=debug for the run.

ana: @eng-runtime (cc @ryan) — can you take the replay tomorrow 09:00UTC? we'll need traces for the high-queue window.

ryan: Ack. I'll schedule the replay at 09:00UTC, run staircase, capture kernel logs and host metrics, and post results here.

qa-jen: After replay, we should also generate a minimal prompt set reduced to a single step to determine if multi-step chaining contributes to token expansion. keep both in the pack.

ana: Thanks everyone. Once replay is done we'll decide whether this is a workload tuning (batching/kv cache) or a runtime regression. I'll update the ticket with the bundle link and next steps. :white_check_mark:
